newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK bourse holds usual vigilance for futures expiry.
newsitem.headline: HK bourse holds usual vigilance for futures expiry.

text.p: The Hong Kong stock exchange said on Friday it was maintaining normal surveillance of trading in advance of the expiry of December Hang Seng Index futures on Monday, a month after November expiry sparked severe volatility.
"It is the normal practice of our division to watch the market for any unusual trading," said David Cheung, an official in the trading division at the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong.

On November 28, the last day of trading of November index futures contracts and options, the Hang Seng Index jumped 213 points to an all-time high of 13,744.30 in the first 15 minutes of trade but finished the day down 220 points.
The exchange said then it was looking into "unusual trading" at the start of the session. Market sources said six brokerage houses were being asked to explain trades made that day.

"The SFC (Securities and Futures Commission) and the stock exchange are still making inquiries into the incident," said Cheung. "The inquiry is ongoing. We haven't finished yet. If there is any wrongdoing, it will be reported."
